subject: Discrepancy in service continuity tally for EdgeChain path (requesting accounting & remedy)
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@acmehealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: ops-team@acmehealth.com
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Discrepancy in November availability tally for EdgeChain path

Hi Mina,

We're reviewing November's monthly availability statement against our internal monitoring and noticed a discrepancy related to the EdgeChain egress path on 2026-11-24. The Redwood portal shows a ~22m partial degradation window for our us-west edge, but our traces (attached) show a longer tail and multiple hit-rate drops that look like the same event stretched across two upstream CDNs.

Can you help reconcile how Redwood attributed the event (maintenance window vs third-party) and whether the partial-degradation logic excluded the second CDN ripple? We need this for our procurement review — if the larger window is considered Redwood-affecting, we'll need to request credit per SOW section 3.2.

Attachments: edgechain-log-20261124.txt, timeline.png (ops export)

Thanks,
Sanjay Rao
Director, Platform Reliability
Acme Health

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 08:23:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discrepancy in November availability tally for EdgeChain path

Mina — I dug into runtime traces and our routing decision logs. Summary:

- 2026-11-24 03:42:10–03:58:30 UTC: Upstream CDN-A reported a maintenance flare that we treat as third-party maintenance for paths where traffic was pinned to that provider. That maps to the ~22m window in the portal.
- 2026-11-24 03:59:05–04:18:45 UTC: After CDN-A started degrading, our smart-router shifted a subset (~37% of ACME traffic) to a failover route that traversed CDN-B. CDN-B experienced a slow drift (increased 5xx rates and response tail latency) that we initially classified as transient partial degradation rather than a provider maintenance window.

Why the portal shows ~22m: currently our availability ledger attributes windowed counts to the initiating path (CDN-A) if the orchestration flagged a formal maintenance marker, and it excludes follow-on slow-degrades on alternate providers unless they cross the partial-degradation SLO threshold for the same route. The effect: the post-failover tail you see in your traces is in our event logs but not always counted toward a single contiguous outage because of the ledger's attribution rules.

Attached a cut of the routing log and annotated timeline: edgechain-log-20261124.txt, edgechain-timeline-annotated.png

Questions for decision:
- Do you want us to re-run the tally treating the failover tail as contiguous with the initiating event for your account (i.e., attribute the entire 36m window to Redwood-affecting availability)?
- If so, we can propose either a full SLA credit per SOW or a pro-rated credit limited to traffic actually routed through Redwood-controlled surfaces (your call).

Markus
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@acmehealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: ops-team@acmehealth.com
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 13:31:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discrepancy in November availability tally for EdgeChain path

Mina / Ben,

Thanks Markus — that explanation helps. For procurement and our internal auditors, we need the final tally to reflect customer-observed continuity. The users experienced degraded responses until 04:18:45 UTC (we have span traces attached). Per SOW 3.2 the spirit of the SLA is continuity of service to end users, not per-provider bookkeeping.

We'd prefer Redwood to re-run the tally to treat the whole sequence as contiguous and apply the SOW credit. If Redwood believes a pro-rated credit is more appropriate, we need a transparent calculation and the routing weighting you used (how the 37% failover fraction was computed).

Please get back to us with:
- Recomputed availability window and credit amount (formula), or
- A clear note if Redwood will not adjust and why (with logs).

Sanjay
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discrepancy in November availability tally for EdgeChain path

Sanjay — I appreciate the clarity and the urgency. Proposal below after conferring with engineering and finance:

1) Re-tally as contiguous: we'll re-run the availability ledger to treat the CDN-A initiation and the subsequent CDN-B tail as a single contiguous event for ACME Health. That will produce a consolidated window of 36m 35s (03:42:10–04:18:45 UTC).

2) Credit approach: because ~37% of your traffic was routed via Redwood-managed failover surfaces (per Markus's routing sample) we propose a pro-rated SLA credit equal to 37% of the credit amount that would apply to a full Redwood service-impact event. The math and raw routing weights are attached and transparent. If ACME prefers a straight full-credit (per spirit of SOW), we can escalate to our commercial leadership to approve a one-off full credit for Nov — but that requires a waiver and signatures (we can move fast if you'd like).

3) Next steps & timeline:
   - Engineering will ship the re-tally and a PDF credit calculation to you by Tue 2026-12-01 EOD PST (ENG-9123).
   - Ben will prepare a commercial note outlining the waiver path should you request full credit.

I've attached the re-tally inputs and the routing-weight spreadsheet for transparency. Let us know whether you want the pro-rated credit or to escalate for full waiver.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Manager, Customer Success — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: edgechain-recount-inputs.csv, routing-weights-ACME-20261124.xlsx
